newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU ministers to mull Singapore WTO, China policy.
newsitem.headline: EU ministers to mull Singapore WTO, China policy.

text.p: European foreign affairs ministers are due on Monday to discuss once again their policy positions ahead of next month's meeting of the World Trade Organisation in Singapore, EU diplomats and officials said.

"This will be another in a long list of discussions which we have had leading up to Singapore on the ninth (of December)," European Commission spokesman Peter Guilford told a Friday news conference, referring to next month's first full meeting of trade chiefs within the World Trade Organisation.

Ministers will also hear a report by European Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan about his recent meetings with Chinese ministers on European Union proposals for China's phased entry to the world trade body.
Guilford said China had invited the EU for bilateral talks in January to discuss detailed issues related to China's accession, as it had the United States.
He made no secret of the obstacles remaining ahead for China talks, whatever the positive noises emerging recently.
"Once we start negotiating, no doubt there will be massive difficulties, there always are," he said.

A British diplomat described Monday's WTO items, part of an agenda which will range from the EU's Turkey policy to its relations with Iran, as a "brief stock taking" exercise in the wake of ministers discussions in Luxembourg on October 29. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
